businessRules.rule: The visitor returns the numbered pass at the desk.
The staff member records the time out against the open visit.
The pass is marked returned and becomes free to issue again. A pass that is not returned is recorded as outstanding, because an unreturned pass is a credential still in circulation.

A visit still open at the end of the day is closed by the security staff, with the departure recorded as unconfirmed rather than left standing. Many visitors will not remember to sign out, and an entry left permanently open makes the log unable to answer who is still on the premises.
A confirmed departure and an unconfirmed one are distinguishable afterwards. Closing a visit is not the same as watching somebody leave.
A visit is never deleted, and neither is a closure. The record of a visit closed unconfirmed is the record that a visitor was not seen leaving.
A visit is found by pass number or by name, since a visitor at the desk will have one or the other.
A visit already closed cannot be closed again.
An outstanding pass is chased and can be retired where it is not recovered, since a numbered pass in circulation that the school cannot account for is a credential.

transitions.condition: The visitor returns the pass and the time out is recorded (BR-1, BR-2).
The visit is still open at the end of the day (BR-4).
The visit closed without the pass coming back (BR-3).
Not recovered. A pass the school cannot account for is retired (BR-9).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Gate → Log a visitor out → Find the visit
basicFlow.userAction: Finds the open visit by the pass number the visitor has returned, or by their name.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns the open visit at this branch.

basicFlow.navigation: Log a visitor out → Record the time out
basicFlow.userAction: Records the time the visitor left.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Closes the visit with the departure recorded as confirmed.

basicFlow.navigation: Log a visitor out → Mark the pass returned
basicFlow.systemResponse: Frees the pass to be issued again.

basicFlow.navigation: Log a visitor out → Pass not returned
basicFlow.userAction: Records the pass as outstanding where it did not come back.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Keeps it out of circulation for reissue, since an unreturned pass is a credential still out there.

basicFlow.userAction: Closes the visits still open at the end of the day.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the departure as unconfirmed rather than leaving the visit standing.

basicFlow.navigation: Gate → Outstanding passes → Retire the pass
basicFlow.userAction: Retires a pass that was never recovered.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Takes the number out of use, since a pass the school cannot account for is a credential.

alternateFlows.condition: The visitor leaves without returning the pass
alternateFlows.navigation: Log a visitor out → Pass not returned
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded as outstanding, because an unreturned pass is a credential still in circulation (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The visitor never signed out at all
alternateFlows.behaviour: The visit is closed with the departure recorded as unconfirmed. Many visitors will not remember to sign out, and an entry left open makes the log useless (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The visitor cannot remember their pass number
alternateFlows.navigation: Log a visitor out → Find the visit by name
alternateFlows.behaviour: The visit is found by name instead, since a visitor at the desk will have one or the other (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: An outstanding pass is recovered later
alternateFlows.behaviour: It comes back into circulation and stops being outstanding (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: An outstanding pass is never recovered
alternateFlows.navigation: Gate → Outstanding passes → Retire the pass
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is retired and the number goes out of use (BR-9).

departures.requirement: Every visit is closed, either by the visitor signing out or by the security staff at the end of the day. An entry left permanently open makes the log unable to answer who is on the premises.
Closing a visit is not the same as watching somebody leave, and the two are never conflated in the record.

departures.aspect: A pass in circulation is not free
departures.requirement: An unreturned pass cannot be issued to anybody else, and is chased or retired.
A visitor is logged out within 15 seconds, since a queue at the gate is how the desk stops using the system.
Visits and pass records carry the same unset retention period as the visitor record itself.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
